apex-metrics.executive_summary: Apex Metrics is a B2B analytics-adjacent company seeking clearer market positioning and a website that produces qualified opportunities. A strategy call revealed strong urgency around differentiation, sales enablement through the site, and marketing autonomy. A phased diagnose-and-build engagement is the best fit while budget is still forming.
apex-metrics.business_context: Lean marketing leadership is collaborating with an economic buyer who wants measurable pipeline impact. The current site is treated as a weak support asset; sales compensates with PDFs. The team wants a foundation they can operate without ticket bottlenecks.
current_challenges: Positioning does not clearly differentiate Apex Metrics from category peers.
Homepage and offer pages fail to explain the offer, forcing sales workarounds.
Marketing cannot ship campaign pages without developer tickets.
business_goals: Increase qualified opportunities originating from the website.
Establish a shared differentiation narrative for sales and marketing.
Give marketing an ownable CMS workflow for landing pages and updates.
key_opportunities: Message architecture and positioning workshop feeding web and sales.
Rewrite of homepage and primary offer pages.
Template-driven WordPress/Webflow build for campaign velocity.
Instrumentation focused on qualified opportunity paths.
Phased scope that matches budget comfort.
risks: Budget not finalized — oversized proposals may stall decision.
Unconfirmed MarTech stack may delay attribution recommendations.
Spring launch window compresses delivery if discovery slips.
information_gaps: Priority ICP segments and converting pages today
SEO vs AI search priority ranking
apex-metrics.recommended_next_step: Run a focused diagnose phase: positioning and message architecture, site and messaging audit, and a phase-one build recommendation — then present a scoped proposal.

framework.note: Evaluation criteria and scoring rules will be configured after SimpliCreative provides process documentation. This POC does not invent proprietary assessment rules.

diagnosis.summary: Apex does not have a website problem in isolation. The call points to a positioning and buyer-path problem that is limiting qualified opportunities and forcing sales to compensate with PDFs. The recommended phase starts by clarifying the message and conversion path before committing to a full build.
diagnosis.primary_friction: Positioning and buyer-path clarity are weakening the website's credibility and qualified-pipeline conversion.

fast_readiness.label: Flexible
fast_readiness.finding: Marketing needs to publish and update pages without engineering tickets.
fast_readiness.suggested_action: Confirm CMS, reusable page modules, and the approval workflow.

fast_readiness.label: Accessible
fast_readiness.finding: Responsive behavior, accessibility baseline, and performance have not been validated in this call.
fast_readiness.suggested_action: Run accessibility, responsive, and performance review during discovery.

fast_readiness.label: Strategic
fast_readiness.finding: Positioning and the core site narrative do not explain differentiation or the buyer path clearly enough.
fast_readiness.suggested_action: Build message architecture, conversion paths, and search-ready content structure.

fast_readiness.label: Trackable
fast_readiness.finding: The team wants qualified opportunities, but first-touch-to-conversion measurement is not defined.
fast_readiness.suggested_action: Define analytics events, attribution fields, and reporting for qualified opportunities.
